sections.name: File setup

sections.why: Likely reason: the date tool is needed for the default access date.

sections.name: normalize_research_record
sections.title: Standard shape for one record
sections.what: Copies each known field from a raw record into the standard shape, fills blanks with defaults, and keeps the untouched original.
sections.why: Likely reason: every saved record then has the same fields.
sections.watch_out: A missing access date is set to the current time, which is not the real access date.

sections.name: normalize_batch
sections.title: Normalizing a whole list
sections.what: Applies the single-record step to every item in a list and returns the new list.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the caller clean a whole batch in one call.
sections.watch_out: If any item is not a dictionary, the error stops the whole batch.

summary: Makes research records follow one fixed set of field names and fills blank fields with defaults, so the database receives consistent records.
purpose: Keeps stored research uniform no matter which source each record came from.
why: Likely reason: records from different scrapers may have different shapes, so one shape is applied before saving.
how: 1. For each record, copies each standard field and uses a default when it is missing. 2. Sets the access date to the current time when none is given. 3. Keeps the original record in a raw field. 4. For a list, applies the same step to every item.
inputs: Raw records as dictionaries from the scrapers.
outputs: Standard records with the fields source_url, title, author, date_accessed, series_name, country, sector, metric, value, unit, note and raw_data.
risks: A missing access date is replaced with the time of normalizing, not the real access time. Missing text fields become empty text, which can look like real data. The raw copy stores the data twice.
debug: If stored dates look recent for old data, check whether the source record had an access date. If a field is blank, check the field name in the source record. Compare the raw field to see what came in.
